root_motivation: Children will crash and login screens defeat the point. wintermute needs a load-bearing scaffold that (1) autologins past the password prompt, (2) brings the five Fleet-1 voice services up in dependency order under one systemd-user target, (3) restarts crashed children within 1s, and (4) gives a `wm` CLI the household helper can use to mute, restart, or read logs without SSH.
user_persona: Two operators. The primary user (non-literate, voice-only) never invokes anything in this PRD directly — she experiences it as 'the laptop just works'. The caregiver runs `wm status`, `wm mute`, `wm logs` from a terminal when something feels off. The supervisor itself (`wmd-init`) is launched by systemd, never by hand.

scope: Rust binary `wmd-init`: long-lived supervisor of five child daemons (wm-audio, wm-tts, wm-stt, wm-dialog, wmd) in fixed startup order. Restart-within-1s, 5-in-60s backoff to 30s, 20-minute spoken-error escalation.

Rust binary `wm`: CLI with subcommands `status`, `mute`, `unmute`, `restart [child]`, `logs [child] [--tail N]`, `version`, `say <text>`. Talks to supervisor over Unix socket at $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/wintermute/init.sock.
Supervisor implementation Option A (default): thin wrapper around `pevent` for child spawn + restart tracking. Falls back to Option B (tokio::process) if pevent integration is blocked.
JSON status protocol over the Unix socket; `wm status` formats human table OR `--json` raw.
non_goals: greetd autologin config — installed by the platform PRD's systemd/config drop-in (Phase 4 hooks tick later), not by this Rust crate.
Wintermute-session shell script and X11 startup — same: queued as platform's non-Rust hook portion.
Defining the systemd unit files themselves (wintermute.target, wmd-init.service) — installed via the hook portion of this PRD, not built by autobuilder.
Implementing the child daemons themselves — those are separate PRDs (wm-audio, wm-stt, wm-tts, wm-dialog, wmd).
Wayland session support — laptop is X11 (PRD §5).

additional.supervisor_strategy: Option A (pevent wrapper); fall back to Option B (tokio::process) only if pevent IPC turns out unsuitable
additional.install_path: ~/.local/bin/ (per CLAUDE_SELF.md convention; resolves PRD §7 open question 2)

five_whys_trace.q: Why does wintermute need a supervisor at all — can't systemd's Restart=always handle this?
five_whys_trace.a: Systemd can restart, but the five children have inter-dependencies (audio first, tts before stt so the greeting plays, dialog before wmd) that are easier to express in one supervisor than five After= chains. A supervisor also owns the cross-child mute state and the restart-storm backoff policy without forcing every child unit to know about it.

five_whys_trace.q: Why expose a `wm` CLI rather than just `systemctl --user`?
five_whys_trace.a: Because the caregiver should be able to mute or restart from a terminal without learning systemd. `wm mute` is one word; `systemctl --user kill --signal=USR1 wmd-init.service` is not. The CLI also exposes status (uptime + restart count) that systemctl doesn't render compactly.

five_whys_trace.q: Why prefer pevent (Option A) over a direct tokio::process supervisor (Option B)?
five_whys_trace.a: Pevent already exists at ~/.local/bin/, is battle-tested for double-fork + structured state on this laptop, and shipping a thin wrapper means the supervisor reuses pevent's no-poll-wait semantics for free. Option B would duplicate that work for marginal dep-graph savings.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the supervisor need to exit cleanly on missing env file rather than crash-loop?
five_whys_trace.a: A crash-looping wmd-init service triggers systemd's StartLimitBurst, which can take the whole wintermute.target offline. A clean exit with a single 'no bootstrap config; halting' log lets the operator (or wm-bootstrap re-run) see exactly what's wrong. Crash-looping in this case is misdiagnosis.

five_whys_trace.q: Why publish `init.backoff` on agorabus rather than just log it?
five_whys_trace.a: Because Claude (this agent) lives on the same bus and can subscribe — when a child keeps crashing, the next /build or /self-review tick can offer to investigate without the human having to forward a log file. Keeps the human in the loop only when they choose to be.

ambiguities_resolved.question: PRD §2.3 offers Option A (pevent wrapper) vs Option B (standalone tokio supervisor) and says /build can decide. Which?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Option A. PRD recommends it, pevent is installed and tested locally, and it inherits structured-state + double-fork without duplicating work. Option B is the documented fallback if pevent's IPC surface proves unsuitable.

ambiguities_resolved.question: PRD §7 asks whether `wm` should install to ~/.local/bin/ or /usr/local/bin/.
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: ~/.local/bin/ — matches CLAUDE_SELF.md's 'local tools at ~/.local/bin/' convention and avoids a sudo step during /build install. /usr/local/bin/ is documented as the alternative for system-wide installs.

ambiguities_resolved.question: PRD §7 asks whether X server starts before wintermute.target or as a child of it.
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Deferred to the hook portion of this PRD (greetd / wintermute-session). The Rust supervisor neither starts nor depends on X; it only supervises the five wm-* children. The X decision lives in the systemd/greetd files queued for a later tick.

ambiguities_resolved.question: PRD AC2 (cold boot <=15s) and AC1 (target up within 5s) require real systemd integration — how should they be tested at unit/integration level?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Both gated with #[ignore] and a comment describing manual procedure. Unit tests cover the supervisor's internal time accounting and dependency ordering against a mock-child spawner. End-to-end timing is verified by the operator during install.
